newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian court sets safe venue for Rao hearings.
newsitem.headline: Indian court sets safe venue for Rao hearings.

text.p: An Indian court on Friday assigned an international conference complex for hearings in cases of forgery and cheating involving former Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao.
The Supreme Court had ordered a safe venue for the two hearings after his lawyers expressed concern over his security in Delhi's crowded trial courts.
The Delhi High Court decided on Vigyan Bhavan, a cavernous centre where Rao once hosted foreign dignitaries at international conferences.
Rao and five others have been charged in a seven-year-old forgery case in which they were alleged to have tried to defame a son of former Prime Minister Vishwanath Pratap Singh.
Rao has not commented publicly on the charges, which carry a maximum prison term of seven years.

He has also been named in a criminal conspiracy case involving the alleged cheating of an Indian businessman of $100,000. Rao, who has not yet been formally charged in the case, has denied the accusation.
Criminal conspiracy to cheat also carries a maximum penalty of seven years in jail.
The cheating case is due for hearing on November 6. The forgery case will be heard on October 30, but Rao was not expected to have to appear in that case until a later date.
